adventure.pitch: A gothic three-act reckoning with a debt the living never meant to inherit. Fifty years ago the valley of Marrowfen was flooded to make a reservoir, and the bell-founder Corvin Vaile was sealed alive inside his half-finished church when the waters rose. His masterpiece bell went down with him. Now, each night, that drowned bell tolls and climbs its own rope, and with every toll it hauls another co

scene:b1.title: The Boathouse at Sillow
scene:b1.summary: The party arrives as the nightly toll begins and drowned corpses surface, some clawing up onto the docks. Terrified villagers led by ferrywoman Mother Sedge beg for help; old lamplighter Gaunt Weem knows the true history but speaks in riddles and rope-knots. Ways in: calm/interrogate the crowd (Persuasion DC 12), read the church records Weem hoards (Investigation DC 13), or fight off the first risen dead crawling ashore. Establish the rising bell and the location of the sunken church.

scenePlan.look: A ramshackle timber shanty-town on stilts along a black reservoir's edge, sagging boardwalks and a leaning boathouse, rowboats tethered to a long dock, dark water studded with pale surfacing bodies.
scenePlan.mood: lantern-lit dusk, cold mist rising off the water
features: the long dock with tethered rowboats
the black waterline where corpses surfac

scene:b2.title: The Drowned Bell-Road
scene:b2.summary: By boat and breath the party descends the old sunken lane toward the church — a submerged street of roofs, a graveyard whose stones have shifted, and the taut bell-rope rising from the depths, hung with drifting dead being hauled upward. Beats: navigate the flooded ruins (Athletics/Survival DC 13), decipher Vaile's foundry-marks to learn the debt (Arcana or History DC 14 — Elara), or slip past the guardian dead (Stealth DC 13 — Pip). Ghoulish drowned things nest in the flooded belfry-yard.

scenePlan.look: An underwater street of drowned rooftops and a sunken graveyard, silt-choked lanes between broken walls, a thick barnacled rope stretching up out of frame with corpses snagged along its length.
scenePlan.mood: green-black gloom pierced by shafts of moonlight through the water
features: Vaile's foundry-mark carved on a lintel

scene:b3.title: Vaile's Bell-Chamber
scene:b3.summary: The half-finished stone church, its air-pocketed nave holding a single trembling breath, the great bell swinging on its rising rope with Vaile's shackled skeleton fused to the clapper. His shade demands the debt paid. Resolutions: give last rites and speak his name aloud into the bell (Religion DC 14), break/recast the bell in the cold foundry-hearth (Arcana or Smith's tools DC 15 — Aldric), or bind him with his own foundry-marks (Arcana DC 15). Fighting the shade alone won't stop the toll — the debt must be acknowledged. Success sinks the dead and stills the water.

scenePlan.look: A flooded stone church with a domed air-pocket nave, a massive dark bell hanging over a cracked altar, a cold foundry-hearth against one wall, chains and a shackled skeleton fused to the bell's clapper.
scenePlan.mood: drowned candle-glow in a trembling air pocket, echoing drips
features: the great swinging bell on its rope

voice.tic: counts the drowned on her knuckles as she speaks
voice.want: to keep her ferry-folk alive one more night
voice.fear: that her own drowned husband is on the rope

voice.tic: ties and unties a knot of rope while talking, never finishing it
voice.want: to unburden the secret he helped bury
voice.fear: being named among those who sealed the church

voice.tic: speaks in the reverberating cadence of a struck bell, each word ringing twice
voice.want: his name spoken and his last rites given
voice.fear: being forgotten again beneath the water

plants.what: Weem's forever-unfinished rope knot mirrors the unfinished bell-rope and the unfinished burial — completing a rite is what settles the debt.
Vaile's foundry-mark, first seen on a Sillow lintel, recurs on the sunken church and can be used to bind or break the bell.
Mother Sedge's drowned husband on the rope — a personal face on the horror that raises the stakes of stopping the toll.
Aldric's grandfather's smith-hammer, family-forged in this very valley, is the tool that can recast the bell in the cold hearth.

pcBackstories.name: Aldric the Fighter
pcBackstories.backstory: Grandson of a valley smith who was pressed into service casting the reservoir's floodgate chains, Aldric carries the family hammer forged in Marrowfen before the drowning. His grandfather never spoke of what was sealed away — Aldric returns to a valley that swallowed his blood's craft, hammer in hand.

pcBackstories.name: Elara the Wizard
pcBackstories.backstory: A scholar of drowned languages and sympathetic resonance, Elara came to Marrowfen chasing a rumor of a bell that rings underwater. Her mentor once studied Vaile's foundry-marks and vanished; she suspects the answer waits in the black church, and dreads finding her mentor's name among the debts.

pcBackstories.name: Pip the Rogue
pcBackstories.backstory: Born in Sillow's shanties after the flood, Pip grew up hearing the muffled toll and looting rooftops the water spared. The dead rising is personal — some of them are neighbors, some kin — and Pip alone knows the shifting lanes of the sunken street by feel.

blueprint.premise: A gothic three-act reckoning with a debt the living never meant to inherit. Fifty years ago the valley of Marrowfen was flooded to make a reservoir, and the bell-founder Corvin Vaile was sealed alive inside his half-finished church when the waters rose. His masterpiece bell went down with him. Now, each night, that drowned bell tolls and climbs its own rope, and with every toll it hauls another co
blueprint.centralProblem: The tolling bell is rising night by night; when it breaches the surface the whole reservoir's dead will walk, and the town that authorized the flooding will drown in its own ancestors. The party must descend to the sunken church and settle Vaile's debt — silence the bell — before it crests.
blueprint.intendedEnding: The party reaches Vaile's flooded bell-chamber, learns the debt is a name unspoken and a burial unfinished, and either recasts/breaks the bell, gives Vaile the last rites and the recognition he was denied, or binds him anew. The tolling stops, the risen dead sink back, and the reservoir goes still — the valley's guilt finally acknowledged rather than merely drowned.
blueprint.opening: Dusk on the shore of Marrowfen Reservoir, in the shanty-town of Sillow that clings to the new waterline. Villagers cluster in a lantern-lit boathouse as the first muffled toll rolls up through the black water and the bodies begin to bob.

spine.intent: Party witnesses the rising bell and the risen dead; accepts the descent.
Party learns Vaile was buried alive and denied his name and rites.
Party pays the debt at the bell-chamber.
The bell falls silent, the dead sink, the valley's guilt is finally acknowledged.
